visual_evidence: Top-right standing piece: red plastic rectangular bar with its upward-facing fracture surface showing a thin outer perimeter shell and a hollow interior crossed by sparse internal infill ribs.
Top-right standing piece: jagged, uneven fracture rim around the perimeter with raised corner peaks and slight whitish stress-whitening along the torn edges, rather than a flat single-layer plane.
Top-left piece: mating red rectangular bar lying flat with a semicircular hole or cutout directly at the broken right end and a stepped fracture face.

Bottom-left and bottom-right pieces: two matching red rectangular pieces with smooth, flat 45-degree angled faces pointing toward each other and no visible rough fracture texture on those angled faces.
diagnosis.probable_cause: Cross-layer overload fracture through the perimeters and sparse infill of an FDM-printed part, initiating at the stress concentration and reduced cross-section of the hole at the break. Unlike pure single-layer delamination, the fracture surface is jagged and exposes the cross-section of the outer perimeter walls and internal sparse infill ribs.
alternative_modes: The exposed fracture on the standing piece is jagged with raised perimeter corner peaks and exposes the cross-section of sparse internal infill ribs rather than separating cleanly along a single flat layer boundary with intact rounded bead tops.

solutions.title: Increase perimeter walls and infill density around the hole
solutions.description: Increase perimeter wall loops from the thin shell visible to 5-6 walls and raise infill density to 50-100% locally (using modifier meshes in the slicer) around the hole so the reduced cross-section is solid rather than hollow.
pros: Eliminates the hollow interior voids seen at the break
Directly reinforces the thin walls around the hole without changing external dimensions
Requires only slicer setting changes with no CAD rework
cons: Increases print time and filament usage

visual.label: Increase wall count and infill density

solutions.title: Reinforce or relocate the hole away from peak stress
solutions.description: Move the hole out of the highest-load section or widen the bar / add a local boss around the hole so the net cross-section matches the rest of the bar.
pros: Removes the geometric weak point where the fracture initiated
Provides continuous load paths around the cutout
cons: Requires modifying the CAD model and checking clearance with mating parts
Adds slight bulk if a local boss is added

solutions.title: Optimize print orientation and layer bonding
solutions.description: Orient the bar on the build plate so continuous perimeter extrusions run uninterrupted along the primary load direction and around the hole, and raise nozzle temperature by 5 to 10 C with reduced cooling fan.
pros: Aligns continuous filament strands with the tensile load path
Improves fusion between perimeters and infill walls
cons: May require support material depending on other part features
Higher nozzle temperature with lower cooling can slightly reduce overhang crispness

solutions.title: Switch to a tougher filament such as PETG or Nylon
solutions.description: Print the part in a higher-toughness, more ductile polymer (such as PETG, ABS, or PA/Nylon) instead of rigid PLA to tolerate stress concentrations at holes without sudden brittle cracking.
pros: Higher impact resistance and elongation before break
Better energy absorption around notches and holes
cons: Higher filament cost and potential need for filament drying or an enclosure
